title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on the Implementation of the Convention on the Recognition and Enforcement of Foreign Arbitral Awards Acceded to by China
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on the Implementation of the Convention on the Recognition and Enforcement of Foreign Arbitral Awards Acceded to by China

Fa (Jing) Fa [1987] No. 5

All Local High People's Courts and Intermediate People's Courts, All Maritime Courts and Railway Transport Intermediate Courts:

At its 18th Session on December 2, 1986, the Standing Committee of the Sixth National People's Congress decided that China would accede to the Convention on the Recognition and Enforcement of Foreign Arbitral Awards adopted in New York in 1958 (hereinafter referred to as the "1958 New York Convention"). The Convention shall enter into force for China on April 22, 1987. All High People's Courts and Intermediate People's Courts shall immediately organize personnel handling economic and civil trials, enforcement personnel, and other relevant persons to earnestly study this important international convention and faithfully implement it in accordance with its provisions. The following notice is hereby issued on several issues concerning the implementation of this Convention:

1. In accordance with the reservation of reciprocity made by China at the time of acceding to the Convention, China shall apply the Convention to the recognition and enforcement of arbitral awards made in the territory of another Contracting State. Where there are differing provisions between the Convention and the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (for Trial Implementation), the provisions of the Convention shall prevail.

For arbitral awards made in the territory of a non-Contracting State that require recognition and enforcement by a Chinese court, the matter shall be handled in accordance with the provisions of Article 204 of the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation).

2. In accordance with the commercial reservation made by China at the time of acceding to the Convention, China shall apply the Convention only to disputes arising from contractual and non-contractual commercial legal relationships as defined by Chinese law. The so-called "contractual and non-contractual commercial legal relationships" specifically refer to economic rights and obligations arising from contracts, torts, or relevant legal provisions, such as sales of goods, property leases, engineering contracts, processing and subcontracting, technology transfer, equity joint ventures, contractual joint ventures, exploration and development of natural resources, insurance, credit, labor services, agency, consulting services, and carriage of passengers and goods by sea, civil aviation, railway, and road, as well as product liability, environmental pollution, maritime accidents, and disputes over ownership, but do not include disputes between foreign investors and host governments.

3. In accordance with Article IV of the 1958 New York Convention, an application to a Chinese court for recognition and enforcement of an arbitral award made in the territory of another Contracting State shall be submitted by a party to the arbitral award. The application shall be accepted by the Intermediate People's Court in any of the following locations in China:

(1) If the person against whom enforcement is sought is a natural person, the place of his domicile or residence;
(2) If the person against whom enforcement is sought is a legal person, the location of its principal place of business;
(3) If the person against whom enforcement is sought has no domicile, residence, or principal place of business in China but has property within China, the location of that property.

4. Upon receiving an application from a party, the competent people's court having jurisdiction in China shall examine the arbitral award for which recognition and enforcement are sought. If it finds that none of the grounds set forth in Article V(1) and (2) of the 1958 New York Convention exist, it shall render an order recognizing the validity of the award and enforcing it in accordance with the procedures prescribed by the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation). If it finds that any of the grounds set forth in Article V(2) exist, or if evidence provided by the person against whom enforcement is sought proves that any of the grounds set forth in Article V(1) exist, it shall render an order dismissing the application and refusing recognition and enforcement.

5. The arbitral awards for which recognition and enforcement are sought from Chinese courts are limited to those made in the territory of another Contracting State after the 1958 New York Convention enters into force for China. Such application shall be submitted within the time limit for applying for enforcement provided for in Article 169 of the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation).

This notice is hereby given and shall be complied with accordingly.

April 10, 1987

Annex I:

Relevant Provisions of the

Convention on the Recognition and Enforcement of Foreign Arbitral Awards

Quoted in this Notice

Article IV

1. To obtain the recognition and enforcement mentioned in the preceding article, the party applying for recognition and enforcement shall, at the time of the application, supply:

(a) The duly authenticated original award or a duly certified copy thereof;
(b) The original agreement referred to in Article II or a duly certified copy thereof.

2. If the said award or agreement is not made in an official language of the country in which the award is relied upon, the party applying for recognition and enforcement of the award shall produce a translation of these documents into such language. The translation shall be certified by an official or sworn translator or by a diplomatic or consular agent.

Article V

1. Recognition and enforcement of the award may be refused, at the request of the party against whom it is invoked, only if that party furnishes to the competent authority where the recognition and enforcement is sought proof that:

(a) The parties to the agreement referred to in Article II were, under the law applicable to them, under some incapacity, or the said agreement is not valid under the law to which the parties have subjected it or, failing any indication thereon, under the law of the country where the award was made; or
(b) The party against whom the award is invoked was not given proper notice of the appointment of the arbitrator or of the arbitration proceedings or was otherwise unable to present his case; or
(c) The award deals with a difference not contemplated by or not falling within the terms of the submission to arbitration, or it contains decisions on matters beyond the scope of the submission to arbitration, provided that, if the decisions on matters submitted to arbitration can be separated from those not so submitted, that part of the award which contains decisions on matters submitted to arbitration may be recognized and enforced; or
(d) The composition of the arbitral authority or the arbitral procedure was not in accordance with the agreement of the parties, or, failing such agreement, was not in accordance with the law of the country where the arbitration took place; or
(e) The award has not yet become binding on the parties, or has been set aside or suspended by a competent authority of the country in which, or under the law of which, that award was made.

2. Recognition and enforcement of an arbitral award may also be refused if the competent authority in the country where recognition and enforcement is sought finds that:

(a) The subject matter of the difference is not capable of settlement by arbitration under the law of that country; or
(b) The recognition or enforcement of the award would be contrary to the public policy of that country.

Annex II:

Relevant Provisions of the

Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (for Trial Implementation)

Quoted in this Notice

Article 169

The time limit for applying for enforcement shall be one year if both parties or one of the parties is an individual, and six months if both parties are enterprises, institutions, organs or organizations.

Article 204

With respect to a legally effective judgment or ruling of a foreign court entrusted for enforcement, the People's Court of the People's Republic of China shall examine it in accordance with international treaties concluded or acceded to by the People's Republic of China or in accordance with the principle of reciprocity, and if it considers that it does not violate the basic principles of the laws of the People's Republic of China or the state and social interests of our country, it shall render an order recognizing its validity and enforce it in accordance with the procedures prescribed by this Law. Otherwise, it shall return the matter to the foreign court.
